title: Travel: John Lennon – London to New York City | 1971
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono travelled from London to New York City on 1 June 1971.

They went to America after a tip-off that Ono’s seven-year-old daughter Kyoko had left Mallorca in Spain and was in Bellport, New York. Lennon and Ono were interviewed at Heathrow Airport by a Daily Mirror reporter, to whom Lennon explained their hopes and plans.

At present, all we know is that Kyoko and her father are somewhere in New York. But we believe we can find them. We think they may be with relatives.
John Lennon

Lennon and Ono gave an impromptu press conference at John F Kennedy International Airport, where they again explained their reasons for the trip. Lennon stressed that it was not a working trip, although some work on Imagine was done towards the end of their stay in the Big Apple.

This was the beginning of a month-long break in the recording sessions for the Imagine album, although mixing took place at Ascot Sound Studios in their absence.

Lennon and Ono remained in New York until 14 July 1971.

Also on this day, Lennon and Ono’s assistant Dan Richter travelled to Palma de Mallorca where the couple had been arrested in April. Richter spoke to a local magistrate regarding the alleged kidnapping of Kyoko, and was informed that the case had been dropped.

Richter was also informed that charges against him had also been dropped, although he had no prior knowledge of them, and had potentially put himself in jeopardy by returning to Spain.
